title: Autoscale-aware mini-batcher with quantization trampoline and graceful fallback
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers running Dedicated/Dedicated-burst see transient latency spikes during autoscale events (node drain/scale-out) where aggressive quantization and static batch shapes either violate SLOs or produce sudden cost jumps. This PR introduces an autoscale-aware mini-batcher that coordinates short-lived microbatch shapes with a quantization "trampoline" strategy: when autoscale or topology changes are detected, the system temporarily ramps quantization conservatively (higher precision) and uses smaller microbatches to maintain latency SLOs, then gradually relaxes to cost-favorable quant profiles as routing stabilizes.

Summary of changes: single continuous description below — implementation details, runtime knobs, and rollout plan are included.

Implementation:
- Runtime: new minibatcher component (services/serving/minibatcher) that exposes an AutoscaleHint API. The minibatcher monitors autoscaler events and node health signals from the orchestration layer, and transitions batch shapes on a per-tenant basis to microbatch lanes when instability is detected.
- Quant trampoline: pkg/quant/trampoline implements a small state machine with three quant tiers (precise, mixed, economical). On autoscale start it steps to "precise" for N requests or T seconds (configurable), then steps down with an exponential backoff to restore economical quant levels. The trampoline uses lightweight calibration heuristics (latency headroom + recent token distribution) to pick the next tier.
- Coordination: a tenant-level policy (cfg/policies/tenant_prefill_policies.go) allows admins to opt-out or tune the hysteresis, warmup window, and max cost uplift. Default is enabled for Dedicated and Private deployments only.
- Observability: new metrics (redwood.batch.autoscale_events, redwood.quant.trampoline_steps, redwood.batch.microbatch_ratio) and traces (minibatcher.transition) added to Console dashboards.
- Safety: graceful fallback added — if minibatcher cannot initialize KV-cache for a microbatch lane within a timeout, it falls back to single-request (no batching) to avoid latency amplification.

Testing:
- Unit tests covering state machine transitions and policy parsing.
- Integration test harness extended to simulate scale-in/scale-out events (benchmark-lab/fixtures/autoscale-scenarios.yaml).
- Load test: synthetic 90th-percentile-latency during simulated node churn improved by ~22% on internal perf lab for a representative configuration (p50: 38ms -> 34ms, p95: 142ms -> 111ms).

Backward compatibility and rollout: default opt-in only on Dedicated and Private (main default false for hosted), feature flag redwood.feature.autoscale_mini_batcher. Canary rollout plan: enable for 5 tenants for 48h with telem gating, then 25 tenants, then broad.

Docs and SDK impact: added docs/observability/minibatcher.md and API extension to SDKs (redwood-sdk-python and typescript client wrappers include a new AutoscaleHint field). Changes are backwards-compatible: clients ignoring the hint see no changes.

Related: ENG-4823 tracks production perf regressions during autoscale; ENG-4987 is a follow-up for per-tenant cost dashboards.

Checklist: 
- [x] Runtime component implemented
- [x] Quant trampoline state machine and heuristics
- [x] Policy knobs and feature flag
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs and dashboard tiles
- [x] Canary rollout plan

Notes: this approach prioritizes latency preservation during transient instability over immediate cost savings; the quant trampoline minimizes long-term cost impact by stepping back to economical tiers as soon as stability is detected.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez (reviewer): Can we avoid global locks when switching microbatch lanes? Concern about contention under high concurrency.
Maya Chen (author): The minibatcher uses per-tenant lock sharding; added comments and a microbenchmark in minibatcher_test.go showing <1% overhead for 10k qps across 128 tenants.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Quant trampoline calibration looks heuristic-heavy. How do we avoid oscillation during noisy autoscaler signals?
Maya Chen (author): Added hysteresis and exponential backoff; included a noise filter (moving median over 5s) before stepping tiers. Also added unit tests that simulate noisy events.
Samir Patel (reviewer): Please add an opt-out for tenants who want cost-first behavior even during autoscale spike.
Maya Chen (author): Added tenant_prefill_policies.go with explicit "cost_first_during_autoscale" boolean; default false for Dedicated/Private, exposed in Console.

Diego Alvarez (approval): Approving after seeing microbench numbers and telemetry additions.
